_meta.description: 2026-07-18 Q&A-engine rebuild: agents now ask real questions directly to Claude (data-center) or Gemini (a specific Notebook-X notebook) — see CLAUDE.md and workers/qa-engine.js. The old per-day CALL-COUNT Claude cap (claude_daily_cap, removed below) is retired in favor of a single shared DOLLAR budget (shared_claude_budget below) tracked in D1's claude_budget_usage table (workers/model-router.js) — the SAME table the chore-automation economy already used, not a new separate one. Routine persona flavor (coworker chat, follow-up phrasing, AI-experience notes, critiques) runs Groq-first with Cloudflare fallback via agent-base.js queryGroqRouted() (renamed 2026-07-19 from the misleadingly-named queryGemini()); Hebrew/bilingual composition (gap notes, Trainee guides) goes direct to Gemini via queryGeminiDirect(), meeting-engine report synthesis calls callGemini() itself, and Notebook-X asks also go direct to Gemini, paced by workers/gemini-pacer.js. Agent 10 (Architect) is dormant — excluded from this flow entirely, not just from routine cases.

_app_search_model_meta: Corrected from the stale 'claude-sonnet-4-6' claim (Guides-feature session) — the owner verified directly that data-center-api runs Sonnet 5 today. This field is documentation only (data-center-api chooses its own model independently); workers/claude-client.js's CLAUDE_MODEL constant, used by the Guides pipeline's own direct Anthropic calls, is the actual source of truth for that pipeline and is set to the same 'claude-sonnet-5'.

shared_claude_budget._meta: Added 2026-07-18, replaces the retired claude_daily_cap (a per-day CALL COUNT, checked against `interactions` rows). This is a per-MONTH DOLLAR cap, checked/recorded via workers/model-router.js's getClaudeBudgetStatus()/recordClaudeSpend() — the exact same D1 claude_budget_usage table and functions the chore-automation economy already used (see chore_automation.claude_budget_usd_per_month below, now the single source of truth for this cap; briefly bumped 4.50 -> 5.00 on 2026-07-18 when the budgets were unified, then restored to 4.50 later that day as a deliberate soft-stop leaving real headroom under the account's own $5/month spend ceiling — the two numbers are distinct mechanisms, software soft-stop vs account hard limit). 'Shared' is not aspirational — office-agent Q&A Claude calls (agents/agent-base.js _askDataCenter()) and chore-automation Claude calls (workers/chore-runner.js) draw from and record against the SAME month row, by design, per this session's explicit instruction not to create a second budget.
shared_claude_budget._max_calls_per_day_meta: Added 2026-07-19 (owner-approved rebalance): hard per-day Claude CALL cap — calls, not questions, so follow-up asks count too. Enforced at BOTH layers: (a) generation time — workers/qa-engine.js generateAssignedDailyBatch() assigns at most this many data-center-targeted questions per generation call (one call per simulated day), overflow re-picked from the notebook-x pool; (b) ask time — agents/agent-base.js _askDataCenter() skips (logged, tool_used 'claude-daily-cap-skip') once today's interactions rows with model_source='claude' reach this count (model-router.js getClaudeCallsToday(), UTC calendar day per this repo's DATE('now') convention — a simulated Israel day spans two UTC dates at the 23:00Z first batch, so the effective worst case is ~cap+first-batch, still well under the monthly soft-stop). Worst case 10 x ~$0.0101 x 31d ~= $3.13/mo vs the $4.50 soft-stop. NOT the same mechanism as the retired claude_daily_cap (30, which gated ALL agent Claude usage before the dollar budget existed); this is a routing-mix control layered UNDER the monthly dollar cap, not a replacement for it.

graduated_rollout_throttle._meta: Added 2026-07-18 for the FIRST LIVE ACTIVATION of the Q&A engine (cron re-enabled the same day, first run 2026-07-19). This is a TEMPORARY graduated-rollout throttle, NOT a permanent volume limit: workers/agent-runner.js's computeDailyQuestionVolume() caps the day's generated question total at ramp_daily_caps[N], where N = calendar days elapsed in Israel time since activation_date_israel (N=0 on the activation day itself). Once N >= ramp_daily_caps.length the throttle is automatically inert — volume returns to the normal budget-driven computation with NO manual step-up needed. The per-call $-budget check (_askDataCenter) and Gemini pacing (gemini-pacer.js) remain the real backstops throughout. Safe to delete this whole block once the ramp window has passed; applyGraduatedRolloutCap() treats a missing block as 'no throttle'.

guides_claude_budget._meta: Added for the Guides feature (workers/guide-engine.js): a SECOND, independent Claude sub-budget alongside shared_claude_budget above — total Anthropic spend rises $5 -> $10/month, split into two $5 sub-budgets each with its own $4.50 soft-stop (matching shared_claude_budget's own headroom convention under the account's real spend ceiling, now effectively $10/month combined). Tracked via the SAME D1 claude_budget_usage table and the SAME workers/model-router.js getClaudeBudgetStatus()/recordClaudeSpend() functions as shared_claude_budget, distinguished by an explicit component:'guides' option (default is 'qa', so every pre-existing caller is untouched) and a distinct month key ('YYYY-MM#guides' vs 'YYYY-MM') — overrun in one sub-budget cannot drain the other. Covers: the Architect's (agent 10) review/finalize pass on each daily draft (workers/claude-client.js, direct Anthropic API, model claude-sonnet-5) plus the weekly Saturday verification pass (same model, +web_search tool). Fail-by-skip on exhaustion, logged, mirroring the existing 'claude-budget-skip' pattern — occasional skipped guide days are expected and acceptable, per the owner's cost approval (one review pass ~=$0.06-0.085/guide, one-revision worst case ~=$0.12-0.17, ~1 guide/day expected $2.50-3.50/month, all-revisions worst case ~=$5.30/month which DOES breach this soft-stop by design — the skip mechanism is load-bearing here, not decorative).

notebook_x_gemini_pacing._meta: Added 2026-07-18. See workers/gemini-pacer.js's header comment for the full reasoning — summary here for anyone reading this config without the code.
notebook_x_gemini_pacing.why_not_a_precise_quota_split: Gemini's free-tier per-minute quota is shared across THREE consumers this repo cannot fully observe: Notebook-X's own backend (live /ask traffic + its weekly gap-analysis job), this office Q&A automation, and other existing Gemini usage in office-AI-agents itself (report synthesis, coworker chat, gap-report composition). With two of the three consumers invisible to this repo, computing an exact 'fair share' would be false precision — the only safe posture is conservative, wide spacing from THIS automation, leaving deliberate headroom rather than trying to use a computed maximum.
notebook_x_gemini_pacing.mechanism: skip-if-too-soon via a KV-tracked last-call timestamp, not an in-Worker blocking sleep — see checkGeminiPacingSlot().

description: Groq and CF AI are free — run agents hard. Claude is paid — capped by shared_claude_budget above ($4.50/month soft-stop shared with chore-automation, under the account's own $5/month spend ceiling), not a per-day call count. Primary purpose: real usage of both production AI systems (Claude, Gemini) surfaces genuine capability gaps.

_meta.description: Per-provider FREE-TIER limits for the task-type routing table (workers/model-router.js, plan Phase 3). Every provider client module (workers/cerebras-client.js, mistral-client.js, cohere-client.js) exports a matching `<PROVIDER>_LIMITS` constant, and scripts/verify-providers.js asserts this block and those constants agree — so changing one alone FAILS the verifier instead of drifting silently. Code and config are two copies of the same fact here on purpose: the client modules deliberately import no JSON, so they can be loaded by a plain `node` verifier.
_meta.the_overtime_rule: EVERY PROVIDER IN THIS BLOCK STAYS ON ITS FREE TIER. `paid: false` is a standing constraint, not a current observation. Any paid usage anywhere — a new provider, an upgraded plan, or an overage on an existing one — requires the owner's EXPLICIT, PER-INSTANCE approval, called 'overtime'. It is never a standing budget and never a monthly allowance: one approval, one instance, asked for at the time. A session or code path that needs paid usage STOPS AND ASKS; it does not spend and report. There is no automatic escalation from a free tier to a paid one, for any provider, ever — a call that would exceed a free tier is refused and logged as `overtime_required`.
_meta.anthropic_is_deliberately_absent: Anthropic does NOT appear in this block, and its absence is load-bearing rather than an omission. This block enumerates providers the ROUTER may select, and Anthropic is never routed and never shuffled — it is reserved for the Architect and genuine data-center Q&A, under the separate shared_claude_budget / guides_claude_budget caps above. Its two live call paths (agents/agent-base.js _askDataCenter() via the APP_API service binding, and workers/claude-client.js's direct Messages API calls for the Guides pipeline) are pre-existing DIRECT callers that never went through the router and are untouched by it. scripts/verify-providers.js asserts no anthropic key exists here.
_meta.cap_periods_added_2026_08_06: A free tier is not always expressed per day, so a provider may carry `requests_per_day` OR `requests_per_month`. workers/task-router.js's capFor() reads whichever is present and buckets that provider's D1 counter to match — '<provider>#YYYY-MM-DD' for daily, '<provider>#YYYY-MM' for monthly. DAILY WINS if both are set, since a daily window is the tighter one. Only `cohere` is monthly today (1000 calls/month on a trial key). Before this, the counter was daily-only and Cohere's monthly allowance had nowhere honest to live: forced into the daily field it would either refuse at ~20 calls/day or let one day drain the month.
_meta.and_nothing_read_the_per_minute_number_f: CORRECTION APPENDED to the note directly below, which is preserved as written (A15). That note is CORRECT about the facts and was WRONG about the consequence. It concludes that cerebras and mistral 'are therefore constrained BY THE MINUTE, and the router's 20s wall-clock pacing ... is the correct mechanism for them'. The 20s floor permits 3 calls per minute. The note's own measured numbers are 1,000/min and 50/min. Those two sentences sat beside each other for ten days without anyone noticing that the mechanism called correct was refusing 99.7% of a limit the same paragraph had just measured. The reason it went unnoticed is structural, not careless: `requests_per_minute` is READ BY NO CODE PATH — `workers/task-router.js capFor()` reads `requests_per_day` and `requests_per_month` only — so filling the measured number in changed nothing observable, and config/model-routing.json's promise that 'the count check takes over automatically' was never tested against a per-MINUTE measurement. MEASURED COST, from the live report_pipeline table on 2026-08-16: a report REVISE issues a second judgment-lane call seconds after the first, the floor denies it, and the backup answers — cerebras reviewed 0 of 7 reports that went through a revision round, and 1 of 13 overall, on a lane where it is the designated PRIMARY. FIXED 2026-08-16 (OB-100): workers/task-router.js `paceSpacingFor()` derives the spacing from this field — 60000/(requests_per_minute x soft_stop_fraction), giving cerebras 100ms and mistral 2000ms — while a provider whose rate is null keeps the 20s floor. `requests_per_day` STAYS NULL for both, and the note below stays the authority on why: no real daily ceiling is published, and a derived one must never be written here. WHAT THIS FIELD NOW MEANS FOR ANYONE EDITING IT: `requests_per_minute` is live and load-bearing. Changing it changes production pacing with no code edit. A null still means UNKNOWN and still buys the conservative 20s floor.
_meta.per_minute_is_the_binding_constraint_whe: ADDED 2026-08-06 after reading real rate-limit headers. `cerebras` and `mistral` both have `requests_per_day: null` NOT because the number is unknown in the old sense, but because NEITHER PROVIDER PUBLISHES A REAL DAILY CEILING. Mistral emits no daily header at all. Cerebras emits x-ratelimit-limit-requests-day 1440000 — which is exactly its 1000/min multiplied by 1440 minutes, i.e. the per-minute limit restated, not an independent daily allowance. Both are therefore constrained BY THE MINUTE, and the router's 20s wall-clock pacing (which a null daily cap keeps switched on) is the correct mechanism for them, not a count-based soft stop. DO NOT copy a derived daily number out of a response header into `requests_per_day` — it reads as a real limit, disables the pacing that is actually protecting the free tier, and sets a soft stop in the hundreds of thousands.
_meta.nulls_are_honest: A null limit means THIS REPO DOES NOT KNOW the number — it does not mean unlimited. Where a real free-tier figure was not established against the live provider this session, it is null with a note rather than a plausible-looking invention, because a cap the router enforces against a number nobody verified is worse than no local cap at all: it refuses real work for a reason that was never true. The router treats null as 'pace conservatively and believe the response headers'. The supervised test procedure (back-office-AI-agents/docs/procedures/) establishes the real values against live APIs before any lane carries volume.
_meta.pre_existing_providers: groq / cloudflare_ai / gemini were already in service before this block existed. `daily_limits` above REMAINS the source of truth for their daily numbers; they are repeated here only so the router sees one uniform provider shape, and verify-providers.js asserts the two agree.

_github_models_removed.was: Judgment / quality lane PRIMARY, secret GITHUB_MODELS_TOKEN, endpoint https://models.github.ai/inference, 8000-token input cap.
_github_models_removed.why: GitHub Models was FULLY RETIRED on 2026-07-30 — playground, catalog, inference API and BYOK, permanently, for all customers. Its catalog and inference endpoints return HTTP 410 even with NO Authorization header, which is what distinguishes a dead service from a rejected credential. Found by the supervised test's Step 1 on 2026-08-06, the first time any model ID in this table was checked against a live catalog.
_github_models_removed.do_not_re_add: The 410 body still says 'temporarily unavailable ... brownout'. That string is stale and outlived the service. Trust the retirement date, not the error text.
_github_models_removed.owner_action_outstanding: CLOSED 2026-08-16 — CORRECTED, appended (A15). The instruction below is kept as written; it is no longer outstanding. `npx wrangler secret list` against the live Worker on 2026-08-16 returns twelve secrets and GITHUB_MODELS_TOKEN is NOT among them, so the owner deleted it at some point after 2026-08-06 and nothing recorded that it had happened. GITHUB_TOKEN IS still present, as required. The generalizable half: an 'owner action outstanding' note has no closer — no session was going to check a secret list to find out, and the item would have read as open indefinitely. Where a config records an action outside a session's authority, it should also record HOW ANYONE WOULD KNOW IT WAS DONE; this one is checkable in one command and nobody ran it for ten days. ORIGINAL TEXT: 'Delete the GITHUB_MODELS_TOKEN secret from the Cloudflare Worker. Not done by any session — no session holds secret-write authority. NOT to be confused with GITHUB_TOKEN, a different secret carrying repo write scope, which is untouched and still required.'
_github_models_removed._kept_as_a_tombstone: This block records a removal rather than vanishing, per the repo's preserve-decision-history rule. It carries no `secret`, `endpoint` or `paid` key, so it is not a provider entry and the verifier's per-provider assertions do not apply to it.

cerebras.role: PRIMARY on BOTH the judgment lane (short scored calls) and the long-document lane (daily report batches). Promoted to judgment on 2026-08-06 when GitHub Models was removed.
cerebras._measured_2026_08_06: These are READ-BACKS from the live API, not estimates. The 131000 input ceiling was established by binary search against gpt-oss-120b: a 130868-token prompt returned 200, a 131018-token prompt returned 400 with 'Current length is 131018 while limit is 131000'. The provider compares against PROMPT length; max_tokens is not added to it. requests_per_minute and tokens_per_minute are from the x-ratelimit-limit-requests-minute / -tokens-minute response headers.
cerebras._why_requests_per_day_is_still_null: THE HEADERS DO CARRY A DAILY NUMBER AND IT IS DELIBERATELY NOT WRITTEN HERE. x-ratelimit-limit-requests-day reports 1440000, which is exactly 1000/min x 1440 min — the per-minute limit multiplied out, which is what a provider emits when it is not publishing a real daily ceiling. Writing it would give the router an 864000-call soft stop: arithmetically valid, meaningless as a limit, and it would silently disable the wall-clock pacing that is currently the only real constraint on this provider. The binding constraint here is REQUESTS PER MINUTE. Null keeps the pacing on. Do not 'fill in the gap' from the header.
cerebras._concentration_risk: One provider, two lanes, and both lanes degrade to the same backup (mistral). Owner-accepted 2026-08-06. Intended diversification if it bites: OpenRouter as a third chat provider — deliberately not added yet.
cerebras._model_note: DEFAULT_MODEL is gpt-oss-120b. The previous value llama-3.3-70b did not exist on this key (404 model_not_found while the same key served a 200 for gpt-oss-120b). The full catalog at that date was three models: gpt-oss-120b, zai-glm-4.7, gemma-4-31b.

mistral.role: BACKUP only, in three lanes — judgment and long-document (both behind cerebras) and Hebrew composition (behind gemini). Primary in none.
mistral._measured_2026_08_06: requests_per_minute 50 and tokens_per_minute 50000 are read-backs from the x-ratelimit-limit-req-minute / x-ratelimit-limit-tokens-minute response headers on a live mistral-small-latest call. mistral-small-latest was confirmed PRESENT in the live catalog (53 models) the same day.
mistral._why_requests_per_day_is_null: Mistral publishes NO daily figure in its response headers — there is no per-day header to read and none was invented. Per-minute is the only rate this repo can actually observe, so it is the binding constraint, and the router's wall-clock pacing stays on for this provider.
mistral._carries_the_backup_load: Now the backup for BOTH cerebras lanes as well as gemini's Hebrew lane. A cerebras outage lands judgment AND long_document on this 50-req/min free tier simultaneously. That is the concentration risk recorded on the cerebras block, seen from the other side.
mistral._hebrew_note: Its Hebrew-composition role is the one carrying real quality risk: Hebrew internal notes are the office's own voice, Gemini is primary there for a reason, and this runs when Gemini is exhausted or paced out. A weaker Hebrew note still beats a skipped one — but the gap is precisely what the Lead QA's cross-embodiment comparison exists to measure, so it gets measured, not assumed. The Front is ENGLISH ONLY, so this lane never touches published content.

cohere.role: Embeddings / semantic search ONLY — never chat, not even as a backup. This lane has NO backup by design.
cohere._measured_2026_08_06: Read-backs from a live v2/embed call on embed-multilingual-v3.0 (confirmed PRESENT in the catalog the same day): x-trial-endpoint-call-limit 100 (per minute), x-endpoint-monthly-call-limit 1000. The call returned a 1024-dimension vector and billed 1 input token.
cohere._THIS_IS_A_TRIAL_KEY_NOT_A_FREE_TIER: The limit header is literally named `x-trial-endpoint-call-limit`. This is a Cohere TRIAL key, which is not the same thing as a free production tier: trial keys are rate-limited harder, are not licensed for production use under Cohere's terms, and can be expired or revoked on a schedule this repo does not control. Recorded here, in the config, because this is where someone checking quota will look — and 'why did embeddings stop working' is a much slower question to answer if this distinction is only in a session log. If the local brain's search ever becomes load-bearing, converting to a production key is an OWNER decision under the overtime rule, not a config edit.
cohere._why_the_cap_is_MONTHLY_and_the_daily_fi: ADDED 2026-08-06. Cohere's allowance is 1000 calls per MONTH — there is no daily figure, and there is no honest way to derive one. Dividing by 30 gives ~33/day, and the router's 60% soft stop would then refuse at ~20 calls/day while 980 monthly calls sat unused; leaving it as a daily number would let a single busy day spend the entire month. So `requests_per_day` stays null and `requests_per_month` carries the real number. workers/task-router.js's capFor() reads whichever field is present and buckets the counter to match ('<provider>#YYYY-MM' instead of '<provider>#YYYY-MM-DD'). This is the ONLY provider in this block on a monthly period.
cohere._no_backup_note: 'Fail, don't degrade' is a CORRECTNESS rule here, not a preference. Vectors from two different embedding models do not share a space, so a similarity score computed across them is meaningless — and meaningless in the worst way, since it still returns a confident-looking number between 0 and 1. Substituting a backup provider would corrupt a search index rather than slow it down.
cohere._no_callers_yet_note: EXPECTED to have zero callers for some time. It exists for two capabilities that are designed but NOT BUILT: the local brain's semantic search over campus/agents/<NN-slug>/adaptations/, and the Lead QA's cross-report comparison (plan items 2.7 and 1.5). It ships now because it ships on the one set of secrets the owner installs once.

groq.role: Routine volume lane PRIMARY (drafts, worker chatter) + classification lane BACKUP. Pre-existing.
groq._source: daily_limits.groq / groq_reset_utc above remain the source of truth; repeated here for a uniform provider shape.

cloudflare_ai.role: Classification / routing lane PRIMARY + routine volume lane BACKUP. Pre-existing; account-scoped AI binding, no secret.
cloudflare_ai._source: daily_limits.cloudflare_ai / cloudflare_fallback above remain the source of truth.

cloudflare_images.role: IMAGE lane, `draft` role — the Designer's default. Added 2026-08-10 (plan 5.1). Account-scoped AI binding, no secret.
cloudflare_images._verified_2026_08_10: The model ID was checked against the LIVE catalog on this account with `npx wrangler ai models` before it was written here — AD-030 check 1, which this project has been burned by four times. flux-1-schnell was present alongside flux-2-klein-4b, flux-2-klein-9b, flux-2-dev, stable-diffusion-xl-base-1.0, stable-diffusion-xl-lightning, dreamshaper-8-lcm, phoenix-1.0 and stable-diffusion-v1-5-inpainting. schnell is chosen because it is a 4-step distilled model and therefore the CHEAPEST per image in a lane whose allowance is shared with two chat lanes: the draft role wants many cheap images, and quality is bought in the polish role.
cloudflare_images._why_requests_per_day_is_null_and_it_is_: The other nulls in this block mean 'the provider publishes no daily figure'. THIS one means A REQUEST COUNT IS THE WRONG UNIT. Workers AI's free allowance is 10,000 NEURONS per day, and a Neuron is not a request — one 1024px image costs many times what one short text completion costs, so any request-count cap written here would be a soft stop against a quantity that does not bind. `neurons_per_day` carries the real limit in the real unit, and `neuron_balance_readable: false` records that nothing inside the Worker can read the balance to enforce it. So the router paces this provider by WALL CLOCK (20s, same floor as gemini-pacer.js), which is the only constraint this repo can actually apply. Do not 'fill in' requests_per_day from an invented conversion.
cloudflare_images._shared_allowance_warning: Every Neuron spent here is a Neuron unavailable to `cloudflare_ai`, which is the CLASSIFICATION lane's primary and ROUTINE_VOLUME's backup. The two get separate `provider_usage` counters because they are different work, but the pool is ONE. Heavy Designer output can degrade two chat lanes, and nothing in the counters will say so — which is why it is said here.

gemini_images.role: IMAGE lane, `polish` role — final touches only, never the default. Added 2026-08-10 (plan 5.1).
gemini_images._verified_2026_08_10: The model ID was read back from the LIVE catalog by `workers/gemini-image-client.js` listImageCapableModels() called FROM INSIDE THE WORKER, with the GEMINI_API_KEY the Worker actually holds — not a key from a .env or a scrollback. AD-030's own words: a secret you cannot read is a secret you cannot verify, so the only meaningful catalog check is the one made by the thing that will make the call. Re-run it any time with `{"type":"image_catalog"}`; it makes no generation call and costs no image quota.
gemini_images._this_is_the_same_key_as_the_gemini_bloc: Not a separate allowance. This is the SAME GEMINI_API_KEY that serves hebrew_composition, report_drafting, the report synthesis and the Notebook-X asks — a key `workers/gemini-pacer.js` already paces at 20s BECAUSE two consumers this repo cannot observe share it (Notebook-X's own backend and its weekly gap-analysis job). Image generation is a THIRD unobservable consumer on it. If gap digests start getting paced out after the Designer has a busy day, this is why, and it is written down so that does not need an incident to discover.
gemini_images._why_requests_per_day_is_null: Gemini's free-tier image request ceiling is not carried in any header this client can read, and no number was invented for it. A null cap means THIS REPO DOES NOT KNOW — never 'unlimited' — so the router paces by wall clock instead of counting. A 429 is treated as the free tier being spent: refused, logged, and NOT degraded to the draft role, because a polish request answered by a fresh draft is a silent substitution. Fill a real number in here and the count check takes over automatically with no code change.
gemini_images._never_a_paid_tier: Image generation is the most likely place in this whole config for a free tier to run out mid-task, which makes it the most likely place for someone to reach for a billing toggle. There is no automatic escalation to a paid tier, for any provider, ever. `overtime_required` is a refusal and paid usage needs the owner's explicit, per-instance approval at the time.

gemini.role: Hebrew composition lane PRIMARY (gap notes, summaries) + report synthesis + Notebook-X asks. Pre-existing.
gemini._source: daily_limits.gemini / gemini_reset_israel / notebook_x_gemini_pacing above remain the source of truth.
gemini._pacing_note: Gemini's free-tier quota is shared with consumers this repo cannot observe (Notebook-X's own backend and its weekly gap-analysis job). workers/gemini-pacer.js's 20s spacing STAYS IN FORCE under routing — routing does not get to spend the headroom that pacing deliberately leaves.

_meta.description: Routing for the TODO.md-driven chore/content-generation automation (config/daily-schedule.json's chore_rotation block, workers/chore-runner.js/model-router.js) — a real feature, separate from the 11-agent Q&A office simulation's own daily flow (workers/qa-engine.js). NOTE: TODO.md itself was deleted from this repo's root in the 2026-07-18 repo-cleanup session; workers/chore-runner.js's fetchTodoSection() fetches it via a raw GitHub URL and degrades to a permanent no-op (ranTask:false, 'no tasks configured') now that it 404s — not a crash, but effectively dormant until TODO.md exists again or this is rewired to read something else.
_meta.relationship_to_case_sim_cap: UPDATED 2026-07-18 — this is now the SAME budget as shared_claude_budget above (top-level), not a separate one. claude_budget_usd_per_month below is the single source of truth both blocks point to; office-agent Q&A Claude calls (agent-base.js) and chore-automation Claude calls both read/write the same D1 claude_budget_usage month row via workers/model-router.js's getClaudeBudgetStatus()/recordClaudeSpend(). The old 11-agent-only per-day CALL-COUNT cap (claude_daily_cap) this note used to contrast against no longer exists.

chore_automation.claude_scope: code-writing tasks and approval/review decisions only, by default. Notebook-X overrides this scope — see notebook_x_override below.
chore_automation.claude_pricing_note: Estimated at current Sonnet 5 intro pricing: $2/M input tokens, $10/M output tokens (workers/model-router.js CLAUDE_PRICING). This changes to $3/M input / $15/M output after 2026-08-31. VERIFIED 2026-08-15 against Anthropic's published models overview (platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/overview): $2/$10 is the live published Sonnet 5 rate today, and $3/$15 is the documented standard rate the introductory price discounts from. Both figures held — the audit's finding (#15 / KFM-19) was never that the numbers were wrong, but that nothing distinguished a checked number from an invented one and nothing would say a word when the switch happened. That is now closed three ways: model-router.js records PRICING_VERIFIED_ON (a date, not a boolean), claudePricingStatus() reports verified:false past the change date, and scripts/verify-routing.js FAILS on 2026-09-01 unless somebody re-verifies. The instruction that used to live in this sentence — 'double check the real published price at that time' — is now a check that will not let itself be forgotten.
chore_automation.gemini_role: expanded — default writer for routine content generation across chore-automation tasks (previously reserved for report synthesis only in the office-simulation economy above).
chore_automation.groq_role: routine/easy sub-tasks only (simple formatting, short lookups, classification) — not full content generation.

notebook_x_override.applies_to: notebook-x project only — other projects (data-center, archive-alpha) use the general chore_automation economy above, unchanged.
notebook_x_override.claude_when: task complexity/quality genuinely demands it. Still drawn from the SAME $4.50/mo claude_budget_usd_per_month cap above — this override does not add a second budget.
notebook_x_override.groq_scope: clearly 'easy' sub-tasks only within Notebook-X work (e.g. simple formatting, short lookups) — never content generation itself.
